item.title: Asian Para Games | China off to flying start as powerlifter Guo breaks world record
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
NAGOYA, Japan, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- The Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games got into full swing on Monday as Chinese athletes produced a dominant opening day. In para powerlifting, Cui Zhe opened China's gold medal account by winning the women's 41kg title, extending her streak to five consecutive Asian Para Games. "I'm so happy to win the first gold for China today. I'm grateful to my country!" she said. Guo Lingling claimed the women's 45kg crown in spectacular fashion, setting a world record with a 126kg lift. Guo, who had previously lifted more than 125kg in training, said she came to Nagoya with the goal of breaking the world record and felt calm during the competition. "I'm very confident about competing at the 2028 Los Angeles Paralympics if my body and form allow," she added. Earlier on Monday, Chen Liuxun secured China's first medal of the Games, taking bronze in the men's 49kg para powerlifting with a best lift of 161kg. China's swimmers capped the day with an impressive haul of 14 golds, 12 silvers and six bronzes, breaking several Games records and sweeping the podium in multiple events. "We always give it our all in the pool. We really want to see three Chinese national flags raised together," said Zheng Tingting, winner of the women's 400m freestyle S8, referring to training alongside silver medalist Zhu Hui and bronze medalist Lu Weiyuan. Chinese athletes also dominated para fencing, taking all four gold medals on offer, and added two golds in para athletics. He Shanshan won the women's 1,500m T11 in a Games-record 4:41.19, while veteran Mi Na, who has competed since Beijing 2008 and focused more on coaching in recent years, captured gold in the women's discus F37/F38. "This Games was another chance to challenge myself," Mi said, pledging to keep pushing her limits. Chinese athletes also shone in other sports, winning two gold medals apiece in para cycling and para judo. In team events, China's women's wheelchair basketball team routed Laos 109-20, while the women's sitting volleyball team swept Iran 3-0. In goalball, the Chinese women's team edged host Japan 1-0 and the men's team defeated South Korea 9-4. ■

item.title: China unveils 2026-2030 advertising industry plan, targets around 10 pct annual growth
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
BEIJING, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- China has issued a development plan for the advertising industry during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), setting an average annual growth target of around 10 percent for the sector. The plan, jointly released by the State Administration for Market Regulation and six other authorities, aims to achieve sustained improvement in the quality of advertising businesses, greater investment in research, development and creativity, and significantly enhanced digital and intelligent capabilities. Over the period, advertising is expected to play a stronger role in supporting industrial upgrading, boosting consumption and advancing the globalization of Chinese brands. The plan also outlines coordinated development among large, medium-sized and small advertising companies, deeper collaboration across the industrial chain, and new progress in regional coordination. It calls for a marked improvement in the quality of advertising works and further refinement of advertising laws and regulations. ■

item.title: China records 7.9-pct growth in cross-border trips in Q3
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
BEIJING, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- Chinese border authorities handled 192 million entries and exits in the third quarter of 2026, up 7.9 percent from a year earlier, officials said on Tuesday. Foreign nationals made 23.27 million border crossings from July to September, up 15.6 percent year on year, according to the National Immigration Administration. Visa-free entries by foreign nationals reached 8.99 million, accounting for 77.5 percent of all entries by foreign nationals, a 24.1 percent increase year on year. Since December 2023, when China launched a trial policy granting unilateral visa exemptions to visitors from six countries, it has expanded unilateral visa-free entry to travelers from 50 countries as of September. The policy allows eligible visitors to stay for up to 30 days. It also extended the visa-free transit period for certain countries from 72 or 144 hours to 240 hours in December 2024. There are 57 eligible countries so far. ■

item.title: China's top economic planner vows more efforts to expand domestic demand
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
BEIJING, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- China's top economic planner said Tuesday it will work with relevant departments to expand domestic demand with greater force and more effective measures. More efforts will be made to vigorously boost consumption, Zuo Gang, an official with the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC), said at a news conference. Authorities will raise the share of public service spending in fiscal expenditure, strengthen inclusive policies that reach consumers directly, and promote the expansion and upgrading of goods consumption, including new energy vehicles and smart products, Zuo said. The push comes as consumption shows signs of steady improvement. Total retail sales of goods and services rose 2.6 percent year-on-year in the first three quarters of 2026, with retail sales of services growing faster than goods and new forms of consumption continuing to emerge, official data showed. Final consumption expenditure contributed more to overall economic growth in the January-September period. Zuo said China will invest in both physical assets and human capital to expand effective investment. Specifically, the NDRC will push for the implementation of the 109 major projects outlined in the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) and the "six networks" initiative, covering water, power, computing, communications, urban underground pipelines and logistics networks, Zuo said. Ultra-long special treasury bond funds will be deployed more effectively, and the new policy-based financial instruments will be used at a faster pace, Zuo said, also vowing stronger support for social welfare, technology innovation, industrial upgrading and security resilience. China's investment is undergoing a profound shift in emphasis from traditional sectors to emerging ones, analysts said, noting that artificial intelligence and new infrastructure will serve as key engines for the next round of effective investment. Official data showed the country's investment in innovation-driven sectors held up well in the first three quarters of 2026, even as overall fixed-asset investment continued to contract. Investment in intellectual property products rose 9.3 percent year-on-year in the January-September period, while investment in high-tech industries grew 4.9 percent. Investment will increasingly serve the development of new quality productive forces and the building of a modern industrial system, with the ultimate results felt in expanded employment, rising incomes and improved living standards, said Liu Yuanchun, president of Shanghai University of Finance and Economics. ■

item.title: China to advance new legislation on cultural heritage protection
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
The State Council Information Office (SCIO) holds a press conference on strengthening cultural heritage protection during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 20, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhang Xiaoyu) BEIJING, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- China will work to advance the formulation of a cultural heritage protection law as part of efforts to better preserve and pass on its cultural heritage, an official said Tuesday. Hu Kaihong, deputy director of the General Office of the Central Commission for Guiding Cultural and Ethical Progress, told a media conference that the move is outlined in the country's first five-year plan dedicated to cultural heritage protection issued in September. The plan calls for improving the legal and regulatory framework and strengthening legal safeguards for various types of cultural heritage, including historic and cultural districts, said Hu, also director of the office of the central commission for cultural heritage protection. Hu said the plan for the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030) prioritizes protection, promotes the rational use of cultural heritage and adheres to the principle of minimal intervention, while strengthening systematic protection and unified oversight. The plan sets a target of fully identifying the country's cultural heritage resources by 2030, with an improved regulatory framework, a stronger body of laws and regulations, and a growing pool of professionals. China is home to 61 UNESCO World Heritage sites, including the Great Wall, the Mogao Caves and the Beijing Central Axis. ■

item.title: Xi congratulates Central Institute of Socialism on 70th founding anniversary
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
BEIJING, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday sent a congratulatory letter to the Central Institute of Socialism, celebrating its 70th founding anniversary. In the letter, Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, praised the institute for training a large number of non-CPC representatives who share the CPC's ideals and work in unity toward common goals, and for making important contributions to consolidating and developing the patriotic united front over the past 70 years. He encouraged the institute to continue strengthening political training, building broad political consensus, and improving the quality of its teaching and research as well as its governance capacity. Xi called on the institute to play a greater role in training talent for the united front, conducting theoretical research and promoting principles and policies, so as to better serve the overall work of the CPC and the country. ■

item.title: Overseas buyer attendance at first phase of China's Canton Fair hits record high
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
This photo taken on Oct. 18, 2026 shows a scene at the venue of the 140th Canton Fair in Guangzhou, south China's Guangdong Province. The on-site exhibition of the first phase of the 140th edition of the China Import and Export Fair, also known as the Canton Fair, concluded here on Monday. As of October 19, the fair has attracted 189,000 overseas buyers from 214 countries and regions, a 13.3 percent increase from the session of the same period last year and a new high, according to the China Foreign Trade Centre (CFTC), the organizer of the fair. (Xinhua/Deng Hua) GUANGZHOU, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- The first phase of the 140th China Import and Export Fair, also known as the Canton Fair, concluded its in-person exhibition on Monday, with overseas buyer attendance reaching a record high. As of Monday, 189,000 overseas buyers from 214 countries and regions had attended, up 13.3 percent from the same period of the previous session, said the China Foreign Trade Center, the fair's organizer. It added that the record turnout highlights the resilience and vitality of China's foreign trade. The first phase, themed "Advanced Manufacturing," covered 520,000 square meters, with more than 25,000 booths and over 12,000 participating enterprises. The exhibition showcased the latest products and technologies across five sectors and 19 exhibition areas, including electronics and home appliances, industrial automation, lighting and electrical equipment, hardware and tools, and new energy vehicles and smart mobility. The fair is divided into three phases, all taking place in Guangzhou, the capital of south China's Guangdong Province, and running through Nov. 4. The second phase, themed "Quality Home Life," will run from Oct. 23 to 27 and feature building materials and furniture, household items, gifts and decorations, among other categories. Serving as a barometer and wind vane of China's foreign trade, this year's fair, marking its 70th anniversary, highlights innovation, intelligence, greater specialization and higher quality. Over the past 70 years, the Canton Fair has grown into China's largest and longest-running international trade event, with the most complete product range, the largest number of buyers and the highest transaction volume. Guangdong, a manufacturing hub and trade powerhouse, on Monday reported that its quarterly foreign trade exceeded 3 trillion yuan (about 446 billion U.S. dollars) for the first time in the third quarter of 2026. The data came as China's foreign trade maintained solid momentum in the first three quarters of 2026. item.title: China's Q3 economy picks up pace, reinforcing role as global growth engine
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
* China's GDP grew 4.5 percent year on year in the third quarter, higher than the second quarter's reading of 4.3 percent, supported by fast-growing new drivers and fresh policy support. * New growth drivers continued to expand, contributing more than 40 percent to China's economic growth in the first three quarters. * More foreign firms are embracing "China Opportunity 2.0," deepening their integration into China's industrial and innovation chains. BEIJING, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- China's economy picked up pace in the third quarter (Q3) of 2026, supported by fast-growing new drivers and fresh policy support, staying on track to meet its annual growth target and remaining a leading engine of global growth. China's gross domestic product (GDP) grew 4.5 percent year on year in Q3, higher than the second quarter's reading of 4.3 percent, data from the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) showed Monday. The world's second-largest economy generated about 107.11 trillion yuan (about 15.94 trillion U.S. dollars) in output during the January-September period, expanding 4.6 percent year on year, according to the NBS. "The national economy forged ahead against pressure and continued to shift toward innovation-driven, high-quality development, with growing positive changes in major indicators," the NBS said in a statement. China has consistently contributed around 30 percent of global economic growth, with IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva saying in January that this contribution is expected to stay at roughly the same level in the coming years. GROWING RESILIENCE Noting that the GDP growth of 4.6 percent in the first three quarters is in line with the country's annual growth target, NBS deputy head Mao Shengyong told a media conference that the economy added 5.7 trillion yuan in output during the period, the largest increase for the same period in the past five years. In the third quarter, GDP growth picked up 0.2 percentage points from the second quarter, while some international institutions expected major economies to grow more slowly in July-September compared to the April-June period, Mao said. There was also a notable rise in momentum on a monthly basis. In September, value-added industrial output rose 5.5 percent year on year, 0.3 percentage points faster than in August, while the services production index gained 4.8 percent, up 0.7 percentage points from the previous month. Retail sales of consumer goods grew 1.1 percent in September, 0.7 percentage points faster than in August, and the surveyed urban unemployment rate edged down 0.1 percentage points from August to 5.2 percent. "Growth momentum showed signs of marginal improvement in September," said Wen Bin, chief economist with China Minsheng Bank, citing faster industrial and services output, a rebound in consumption and an initial stabilization of investment. China will step up efforts to expand domestic demand, improve supply, and make macro policies more effective to sustain the positive momentum of innovation-led and high-quality development, Mao said. To this end, China has recently rolled out a batch of new policies, including financial and fiscal support. "With existing policies being implemented faster and incremental policies gradually taking effect, the economy is expected to continue improving in the fourth quarter," Wen said. NEW DRIVERS AT WORK New growth drivers continued to expand, contributing more than 40 percent to China's economic growth in the first three quarters. Value-added industrial output rose 5.3 percent year on year, with equipment manufacturing up 10.2 percent and high-tech manufacturing up 14.3 percent. Output of industrial robots, lithium-ion batteries and 3D printing equipment jumped 29.1 percent, 39.5 percent and 62.5 percent, respectively. Monday's data also showed that the services sector expanded 5.2 percent year on year in the first three quarters, with information transmission, software and IT services up 10.4 percent, and leasing and business services up 12.3 percent. The shift is visible in the economic structure. Manufacturing accounted for 25.7 percent of GDP in the first three quarters, up 0.6 percentage points from a year earlier, while the share of high-tech manufacturing in the value-added output of major industrial enterprises rose 1.6 percentage points. Investment in intellectual property products climbed 9.3 percent. Traditional industries are also moving up the value chain. In Jingdezhen, a ceramics hub in east China's Jiangxi Province, local producers have embraced 3D printing in pottery making, propelling the sector's output to over 100 billion yuan. Meanwhile, some coal mining companies have implemented smart monitoring systems for underground operations, increasing efficiency by 30 percent. Green development is creating openings as well. The penetration rate of new energy vehicles in China has stayed above 60 percent for six consecutive months, while the country's energy consumption per unit of GDP fell 3.1 percent in the first three quarters. "The foundations of the economy remain solid, while new quality productive forces, modern services and high-tech foreign trade are steadily taking root," said Zhu Qigui, associate director of the China Academy of Financial Research. "As long as China continues to rely on innovation, reform and its vast market, the trend of moving toward new and better development will not change," the scholar said. SHARED OPPORTUNITIES A major trading partner of as many as 169 countries and regions, China saw its goods trade rise 18.8 percent year on year to 39.94 trillion yuan in the first three quarters. In September alone, trade grew 27.5 percent. In the first nine months, exports of mechanical and electrical products climbed 23.7 percent and accounted for 64.3 percent of total exports, while intermediate goods made up more than half of all exports, reinforcing China's role as a stabilizing anchor for global industrial and supply chains. In east China's Anhui Province, robotics manufacturer EFORT Intelligent Robot Co., Ltd. has continued to see growth in overseas orders this year, with a batch of its spraying robots set to be exported to Italy. The company's overseas revenue increased by more than 50 percent year on year in the first half of 2026. Meanwhile, the company's client, German automobile giant Volkswagen, is shifting its strategy from "in China, for China" to "in China, beyond China," with cars produced in China already exported to the Middle East and Central Asia. Foreign-invested enterprises in China remained active players in the January-September period, with their imports and exports rising 19 percent to 11.69 trillion yuan, a record high for the same period. Their trade in intermediate goods grew 27.4 percent to 7.9 trillion yuan, and their high-tech product exports jumped 42.1 percent. More foreign firms are embracing "China Opportunity 2.0," deepening their integration into China's industrial and innovation chains, Mao said. ■ (Video editors: Hong Liang and Zhu Cong)
